newsitem.title: CANADA: Air Canada unit attendants reject deal.
newsitem.headline: Air Canada unit attendants reject deal.

text.p: Flight attendants at Air Ontario, one of Air Canada's regional airlines, voted late Thursday to reject a tentative agreement the airline reached with the Canadian Union of Public Employees, Air Ontario said on Friday.
"We are very disappointed with the result of the ratification vote. We believe that the agreement offered was fair and comprehensive," said Air Ontario President Stephen Smith in a statement.
A statement from the union called the deal an "offer" rather than a "tentative agreement".
"The offer was presented to the negotiating committee without a recommendation," CUPE said.
Union members returned to the picket lines in Toronto immediately and will soon be returning to picketing in London, Ontario.
Air Ontario said it will continue operating its planned schedule on Friday, with the contract carriers that it has employed since January 10.
On Saturday, March 15, the airline will phase in its own aircraft and pilots, using the services of Ministry of Transportation-trained replacement flight attendants.
The company said it has withdrawn the tentative agreement and no talks have been planned with CUPE.
CUPE represents 146 flight attendants at the regional airline. They have been on strike since January 5.
